# PickWorth

> PickWorth is an independent review site that hands-on tests AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Grok, Perplexity and more).
> Honest, price-verified verdicts, head-to-head comparisons, and best-of lists, written by a single editorial team.
> No ads in reviews, no paid placement. Method: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/how-we-test-ai-tools/

## Core Pages
- [Home](https://www.pickworth.top/): Know which AI tools are actually worth paying for.
- [Tool Reviews](https://www.pickworth.top/tools/): Reviews of ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Grok, and Perplexity with verified prices and our 0-5 score.
- [Comparisons](https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/): Head-to-head matchups scored per dimension, with the cost question answered.
- [Best-Of Lists](https://www.pickworth.top/lists/): Buyer's guides that pick the right tool by your actual job, not the loudest marketing.
- [Journal](https://www.pickworth.top/blog/): Essays on how we test, why prices move, and when open source matters.
- [About](https://www.pickworth.top/about/): Editorial standards, who funds the site, and why funding never touches the verdicts.
- [Privacy](https://www.pickworth.top/privacy/): What we collect, how cookies and advertising work, and your privacy rights.
- [Contact](https://www.pickworth.top/contact/): Report an error or request a comparison.

- [Cursor Review 2026: Best for Daily Coding, Until the Credits Run Out]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/cursor/ - Cursor review 2026: best AI-native editor for multi-file work and codebase context, with agent mode and model choice. Slips on billing, autonomy, privacy.
- [DeepSeek: the Price Floor of AI Coding]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/deepseek/ - DeepSeek review where the open-weights model earns its cost, where the free chat tier actually runs out, and what the API pricing means for production.

- [Adobe Firefly Review: The Commercially Safe Pick, Not the Most Creative One]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/firefly/ - Adobe Firefly review: the commercially-safe option in AI generation. Where it leads for business and client work, what the credit system actually covers, and how it stacks against Midjourney.
- [Gamma Review: The Fastest Deck in Sixty Seconds, Not the Last Word]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/gamma/ - Gamma review: the fastest way from a blank page to a polished presentation, website or document. Where it wins on speed, where the card format and PowerPoint export cost you, and what the free tier really covers.
- [Google Gemini: the Only Assistant That Reads Your Mail]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/gemini/ - Google Gemini review, where it leads on research, long documents and the Google ecosystem, where the free tier caps you, and which of the four plans is actually worth paying for.
- [GitHub Copilot: Most Accessible, Most Underused]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/github-copilot/ - GitHub Copilot review where it leads on inline completion and in-editor help, where the free tier caps out, and which plan is actually worth paying for, including the student and open-source routes.
- [Grok Knows What Just Happened. That Is Its Whole Job]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/grok/ - Grok review what the live-X knowledge actually buys, where the open-weights and coding tools are going, and the trust questions a buyer should ask.
- [Higgsfield Review: Many Video Models and Real Camera Moves, at an Aggregator Markup]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/higgsfield/ - Higgsfield review: the aggregator that puts many AI video models under one subscription and adds cinematic camera presets. Where it earns its place, what the credit markup really costs, and who should skip it.
- [Kimi Review 2026: Reads a Whole Book, Free, With a Metering Catch]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/kimi/ - Kimi review: Moonshot AI's long-context assistant with a million-token window and a free flagship model. Where it leads, where it slips, and who should use it.
- [Kling AI Review 2026: Best Free Motion Video, Until the Credits Run Out]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/kling/ - Kling AI review: where Kuaishou's video model leads on realistic motion and free entry, what the credit system and free plan actually cost, and how it stacks against Luma and Runway.
- [Luma Review 2026: The Best Camera Control, Weaker on Free]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/luma/ - Luma Dream Machine review: keyframe camera control and cinematic image-to-video lead the category, but the free plan is thin and credits burn on re-rolls.
- [Midjourney Review 2026: Still the Best for Art, But Costs More Than the Hype]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/midjourney/ - Midjourney review: the AI image quality leader, subscription-only with no free tier, from $10 a month, and private generation locked behind the $60 Pro plan.
- [Mistral Le Chat Review 2026: Cheapest Premium Plan, Holds Up on Speed]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/mistral/ - Mistral Le Chat review: the EU-hosted ChatGPT alternative with a generous free tier, Flash Answers speed, open weights, and GDPR appeal, plus where it trails US rivals.
- [Notion AI Review 2026: Best in Notion, Weak Everywhere Else]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/notion-ai/ - Notion AI review: workspace Q&A, meeting notes and database autofill are genuinely useful, but writing trails ChatGPT and the free trial is thin. We score it 3.8 out of 5.
- [Perplexity: One Page Instead of Five Tabs]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/perplexity/ - Perplexity review where the AI search engine beats a normal search box, where its free tier actually runs out, and what the Pro tier is worth.
- [Qwen Review 2026: Free and Open, But Not What You'd Use for English Prose]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/qwen/ - Qwen review of Alibaba's open-weight models and free Qwen Chat: coding, multilingual strength, 256K context, API pricing, and where it trails ChatGPT and Claude.
- [Runway Review 2026: Best for Finished Video, 125-Credit Free Taste]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/runway/ - Runway review, the US pioneer's Gen-4.5 and Aleph editing, where its control and editor lead, why the free tier and credit burn hold it back, and how it stacks against Kling and Luma.
- [Suno Review 2026: Best for Fast Songs, Free Layer Has No Downloads]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/suno/ - Suno review: text-to-song generator that builds a full track with vocals from a prompt. What the free tier caps, Pro/Premier rights, and how it stacks vs Udio.
- [Vercel v0 Review: Cleanest React in the Category, Until You Need a Database]: https://www.pickworth.top/tools/v0/ - Vercel v0 review: the fastest 0-to-1 path from a prompt or screenshot to deployable React and Next.js. Where it wins on clean frontend, where it needs a backend, and what the credit system really costs.

- [Claude Code vs Codex: Better Brains, But Half the Tokens, Is the Answer]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/claude-code-vs-codex/ - Claude Code vs Codex in 2026: Claude Code reasons better, Codex costs far less and writes all day. Where each wins on a real task, and why the 2026 consensus is to run both.
- [Claude Code vs DeepSeek: The Deep Agent Against the Cheap Model]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/claude-code-vs-deepseek/ - Claude Code vs DeepSeek in 2026: the deeper closed agent that handles the hard work, against the open model that costs a fraction and runs on your own hardware. Where each one wins, and how to route between them.
- [Cursor vs Claude Code in 2026: Daily Coding vs Autonomy]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/cursor-vs-claude-code/ - Cursor and Claude Code compared on interface, agent power, model choice and cost. We rate the AI-first editor against Anthropic's terminal agent and say who should use each.
- [DeepSeek vs Claude: a Pricing Argument in a Capability Costume]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/deepseek-vs-claude/ - DeepSeek vs Claude for coding: the open-weights challenger that keeps the price floor low, against the paid tool with the stronger agent story.
- [DeepSeek vs Qwen in 2026: Cheaper Reasoning vs Wider Coverage]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/deepseek-vs-qwen/ - Two open-weights Chinese LLM families face off on reasoning, coding, multilingual reach, API price and open-weight breadth. Our 2026 pick, with a side-by-side table.
- [GitHub Copilot vs Cursor: Half the Price, or the Better AI]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/github-copilot-vs-cursor/ - GitHub Copilot vs Cursor in 2026: Copilot is cheaper and stays in your editor, Cursor is the stronger AI on the hard tasks. Where each wins, and why most teams should start with Copilot.
- [Grok vs ChatGPT: Live Firehose vs Everything Else]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/grok-vs-chatgpt/ - Grok vs ChatGPT, scored on live X knowledge, the free tier, coding and general ability. Where Grok wins, and where the general assistant still wins.
- [Grok vs Gemini: The Live Signal Against the Whole Toolkit]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/grok-vs-gemini/ - Grok vs Gemini in 2026: Grok is the real-time social specialist and the cheaper per-token pick, Gemini is the broader assistant with the bigger context and the Google Workspace integration. Where each one actually wins.
- [Midjourney vs ChatGPT for Images in 2026: Better Art vs Words That Stick]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/midjourney-vs-chatgpt/ - Midjourney vs ChatGPT for image generation in 2026: we compare output quality, free tiers, price, prompt adherence and editing to pick the better AI image tool.
- [Midjourney vs DALL-E: One Looks Better, One Is More Right]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/midjourney-vs-dalle/ - Midjourney vs DALL-E in 2026: Midjourney wins the image that has to be striking, DALL-E wins the one that has to be precise, and text in the image. Where each leads and what each costs.
- [Notion AI vs ChatGPT: The $10 Add-On Everyone Still Compares Is Gone]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/notion-ai-vs-chatgpt/ - Notion AI vs ChatGPT in 2026: full Notion AI now sits in the $20 Business seat, not the old add-on. Where each wins, what the agent credits really cost, and how to pick.
- [Perplexity vs ChatGPT: Not the Same Kind of Tool]: https://www.pickworth.top/comparisons/perplexity-vs-chatgpt/ - Perplexity vs ChatGPT: the answer engine that cites its sources against the general assistant that does the rest. Where each wins, and what each costs.

## Journal & Analysis
- [The Headline Number Is Marketing]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/context-windows-explained/ - What a context window actually does, why a bigger one is not automatically better, and the two questions that decide whether it matters for your work.
- [The Student Route Costs Nothing, and It Is Not a Trial]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/get-github-copilot-pro-free/ - The free tier is not the only free option: verified students, teachers, and maintainers of popular open-source projects get the full Pro plan at $0. How to check eligibility and claim it, and what the free grant actually covers.
- [Three Prompts, Repeated Until a Lucky Run Cannot Win]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/how-we-test-ai-tools/ - Our testing method, written out in full: the fixed prompt set, the repetition problem, the limits we measure and the claims we refuse to repeat.
- [The Token Count Is Not the Quality]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/longer-context-is-not-better/ - Why a bigger context window is not a better tool: capacity is not usefulness. When long context genuinely helps, and when a smaller, focused one beats it.
- [Why No 'Best AI Tool' List Is Ever Wrong About You]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/pick-by-the-job/ - Leaderboards put tools doing different jobs on one scale and force a winner. How to pick by the job you actually do, not by a number that averages away your use case.
- [One Subscription Covers Most People. Here Is the Test]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/the-20-dollar-rule/ - One $20 subscription covers most people's AI needs; a second earns its place only for a specific job. The rule we use to decide when to add a tool.
- [You Are Already Paying for the Tool You Keep Using for Free]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/the-free-tier-you-ignore/ - The quiet overpay in AI tool spending: upgrading a subscription when the free tier already does the job. How to test whether a paid tier is actually buying you anything before you renew.
- [The Markup Does Not Exist That Is the Point]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/the-markup-that-doesnt-exist/ - The strongest case for open-source coding agents is not quality; it is the markup you stop paying. Why a free terminal agent that costs only model tokens is the honestly-priced tool.
- [Four Conditions Matter. The Label Does Not]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/when-open-source-matters/ - Open weights are not automatically better. The four conditions under which open source genuinely changes the decision and when it is just preference.
- [Your Meetings Are a Data Decision, Not a Productivity One]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/where-your-meetings-go/ - The two questions an AI meeting assistant actually raises: does the bot break client trust, and where does the recording live after you cancel? Why privacy can outrank accuracy in the pick.
- [The Free Tier Is the One the Vendor Will Cut]: https://www.pickworth.top/blog/why-prices-move/ - The repricing pattern in AI tools: a generous launch, a quiet tightening, then a restructured tier. How to buy without getting caught.
